We prefer a written response we can attach to our vendor file; a redline-friendly PDF is attached (TerraNova_Security_Questionnaire.pdf). If possible, can you provide answers by EOD Friday (Oct 9)?

Aisha — thanks, and hi Marcus / Neha / Priyom. Below are consolidated answers to the specific sections you highlighted. I’ve kept the language tight so you can paste into your questionnaire; we’ll also attach a filled PDF and a diagram.

1) Data domicile (hosted API)
- Default behavior: Customers select a region when creating an API key/project; persistent customer data (request/response artifacts, indexable metadata, long-term logs) are stored only in the selected region(s). For TerraNova we can pin your hosted tenant to EU (Frankfurt/AMS) so persisted data remains in EU physical infrastructure.
- Ephemeral processing: Transient in-memory artifacts (KV cache, runtime buffers) may exist briefly on nodes outside the EU during autoscaling bursts or cross-region routing for latency mitigation. These artifacts are ephemeral and not written to durable storage. If strict EU-only processing is required, we recommend Redwood Private or a Dedicated region pin with cross-region routing disabled.

2) Retention windows (hosted API)
- Request payloads (customer content): Retained by default for 30 days for diagnostics and model quality monitoring. You can request shorter retention or immediate deletion at onboarding (options: 0d, 7d, 30d).
- Application logs (API access logs, error traces): Retained 365 days for operational purposes and security investigations.
- Audit logs (user-level actions in Console): Retained 365 days; exports can be provided on request.
- Backups & snapshots: Backups of durable stores are retained for a rolling 90-day period. Backups are geo-redundant within the region and are subject to the same regional constraints when you select EU-only.

3) Deletion / erasure process
- Self-service: The Console provides a tenant-level data erasure request form and API endpoint to initiate a deletion.
- Workflow: Once an erasure request is submitted, the system marks the tenant objects for deletion, purges active storage slices, and triggers a background job to remove objects from replicas and indexed caches.
- SLA: Standard hosted API erasure SLA is 72 business hours to complete removal from active storage and indexes. Removal from backups is handled by the backup retention lifecycle (see backups note below).
- Evidence: We provide a deletion certificate that includes the purge job ID, timestamp, and a cryptographic hash of the removed object set upon completion.

4) Backups, replicas, and failover
- Backups are created within the selected region and held for 90 days; they are encrypted at rest. Because backups are immutable snapshots used for disaster recovery, individual backup files cannot be modified or selectively removed prior to retention expiry. If TerraNova requires shorter backup retention or quarantine-based handling, we can implement a contract-level process (e.g., reduce backup retention to 30 days for your tenant and produce monthly backup inventory exports).
- Replication: Active replicas for high availability reside in the same EU region by default when tenant is region-pinned. Cross-region replication will not be enabled for TerraNova unless expressly configured in your account.

5) Exceptions / legal hold
- We will not purge data subject to a legal hold. Legal holds must be communicated through our legal channel and we will preserve the data until the hold is lifted; we will provide the usual audit trail.

6) Cryptography & key management
- All persisted data is encrypted at rest using customer-specific keys (AES-256). We support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-supplied KMS (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / GCP KMS). In the case of customer-managed keys, destroying the key will render persisted backups and snapshots irrecoverable.

7) Evidence / artifacts we can provide
- Completed questionnaire PDF (attached)
- Architecture/region diagram (attached: redwood-residency-diagram.png)
- Deletion certificate (upon completion of any erasure job)
- Audit log export (per request; CSV)
- SOC 2 Type II annual report (redacted) — available under NDA.

Notes and recommended commitments for TerraNova:
- We recommend EU tenant pin + disable cross-region routing to meet strict EU-only requirements for persisted data.
- Consider selecting a 7-day retention for request payloads if you want a tighter window than our default 30 days.

Attachments: redwood-residency-diagram.png (PNG, 1 page), redwood-qna-answers-tn.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

If you’d like, we can convert any of the above bullets into the exact wording for your questionnaire. Happy to hop on a call Thursday morning CET to align.

—Kimberly Park

Redwood Inference

Thanks Kim — that level of detail is helpful. A few follow-ups from our security review team:

1) Backups: we need confirmation that backups containing TerraNova customer content will not be replicated outside the EU under any normal operating mode, and a note on how you handle backup restores that might pull data into a restore target outside region.
2) Deletion evidence: the deletion certificate is perfect — can you confirm the certificate will include the backup snapshot IDs and retention windows so we can reason about residual artifacts?
3) Sandbox environments: we need sandbox/test environments to be flagged as non-production and be able to opt out of logging/content retention for PII.

If you can add a short paragraph clarifying each point above in the final PDF that’ll be great. We’re targeting a vendor approval on Oct 15.

Best,
Aisha

Aisha — quick wrap-up for your vendor file and next steps:

Summary commitments (TerraNova tenant in hosted API):
- Tenant region: EU-only (Frankfurt) for all persisted artifacts (requests, indexes, audit logs).
- Backups: Stored and encrypted within EU; rolling 90-day retention by default. No cross-region replication unless requested in contract.
- Deletion SLA: 72 business hours for active data and indexes; backups removed per retention lifecycle (we can reduce retention to 30 days via contract amendment).
- Evidence: We’ll provide a completed PDF, region diagram, SOC2 summary under NDA, and deletion certificates upon any erasure request.

Next steps:
1) We attached the completed questionnaire (redwood-qna-answers-tn.pdf) and the residency diagram. Please review and confirm whether you want the backup retention set to 30 days (we’ll include that in your tenant configuration and the DPA amendment).
2) If you want to discuss the sandbox/non-prod opt-outs, Kim and Neha are available Thursday CET — please propose a slot.

I’ll follow up in HubSpot with the deal/contract items and the DPA amendment link.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting TerraNova onboarded.
